content:
Following the release of the seventh developer beta for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and other upcoming Apple software updates, Apple is now rolling out the corresponding public beta. Here's everything you need to know.

Apple launches new public beta

Apple earlier today released the following versions:

  • iOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 7 (build number: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 developer beta 7 (build number: 24R5358a)

Apple is now opening up the corresponding versions to public beta testers — this is the fifth public beta. To date, Apple has released new public betas for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's releases don't contain any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official rollout in a few weeks.

Additionally, following the release of the corresponding developer release candidate earlier this morning, Apple has also rolled out the second public release candidate for macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20). The second public release candidate for macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is expected to be available shortly. (Available as of 7:42 PM ET.)

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers match those of the corresponding developer versions.

Enroll in the Apple Public Beta program

If you'd like to register your device for the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the appropriate steps for each device. Here's how to install the public beta on your iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, then choose Sign Up or Sign In.
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone. Then accept the program terms and register your account.
  • Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta".
  • Return to the Software Update screen and tap "Update Now" when the beta version appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, be sure to make a recent backup first.

Have you spotted any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
